title: CRUD API: Build a CRUD REST API with Proper Status Codes
problem_statement:
Build a RESTful API that follows REST principles and implements CRUD operations with proper HTTP status codes. The API should manage a simple resource (e.g., products or articles).

Requirements:

1. Resource definition:
   - Choose a resource (e.g., products, articles, books)
   - Define the resource schema with at least 4 fields:
     - id (unique identifier)
     - name/title (string)
     - description/body (string)
     - createdAt (timestamp)

2. CRUD operations:
   - CREATE: POST /api/resource - Create a new resource
   - READ: GET /api/resource - Get all resources (with pagination)
   - READ: GET /api/resource/:id - Get a specific resource by ID
   - UPDATE: PUT /api/resource/:id - Update a resource (full update)
   - DELETE: DELETE /api/resource/:id - Delete a resource

3. HTTP status codes:
   - 200 OK - Successful GET, PUT, DELETE
   - 201 Created - Successful POST
   - 400 Bad Request - Invalid request data
   - 404 Not Found - Resource not found
   - 405 Method Not Allowed - Unsupported HTTP method
   - 500 Internal Server Error - Server errors

4. REST principles:
   - Use nouns for resource names (not verbs)
   - Use plural nouns for collections (/api/products)
   - Use HTTP methods correctly (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
   - Return JSON responses
   - Use proper content-type header (application/json)

5. Data storage:
   - Use in-memory array for simplicity
   - Generate IDs automatically

Use Express.js. Do not use databases or ORMs.
instructions: Submit exactly one file containing the complete REST API implementation. Include all CRUD operations, proper status codes, and adherence to REST principles. Separate each route using clear comments. Include a brief explanation of the REST principles followed. Do not submit a folder or ZIP.

rubrics.full: Implements all CRUD operations (CREATE, READ all, READ by ID, UPDATE, DELETE) with correct HTTP methods and route patterns.
rubrics.partial: Implements most CRUD operations but has missing operations or incorrect HTTP methods.
rubrics.zero: CRUD operations are missing or incorrectly implemented.

rubrics.full: Uses appropriate HTTP status codes for all scenarios (200, 201, 400, 404, 405, 500) based on the outcome of each operation.
rubrics.partial: Uses status codes but has incorrect codes for some scenarios or missing codes.
rubrics.zero: HTTP status codes are incorrect or not used.

rubrics.full: Follows REST principles: uses nouns for resources, plural for collections, correct HTTP methods, JSON responses, and proper content-type.
rubrics.partial: Mostly follows REST principles but has some violations (e.g., verbs in URLs, wrong methods).
rubrics.zero: Does not follow REST principles or has significant violations.

rubrics.full: Returns consistent JSON responses, handles data validation correctly, generates IDs automatically, and the data structure is well-defined.
rubrics.partial: Response format is mostly correct but has inconsistencies or data handling issues.
rubrics.zero: Response format is incorrect or data handling is flawed.

valid_alternatives: Use PATCH instead of PUT for partial updates (both are acceptable).
Choose any resource type (products, articles, books, etc.) as long as the schema is well-defined.
Add additional fields to the resource schema if desired.
Use different ID generation strategy as long as it ensures uniqueness.
mistakes_to_check: Using verbs in URL paths (e.g., /api/getProducts) instead of nouns (REST principles).
Using wrong HTTP methods for operations (e.g., GET for creating resources) (HTTP methods).
Not returning appropriate status codes (e.g., returning 200 for creation instead of 201) (Status codes).
Not setting Content-Type header to application/json (Response headers).
Using singular nouns for collections (e.g., /api/product instead of /api/products) (REST conventions).
Not validating request data or handling invalid data (Data validation).
